notes: The image's breadboard rows j-f (upper half) are mapped to bank 'b' and rows e-a (lower half) to bank 't', matching the catalogue's row-letter naming; columns are counted from the image labels.
Bottom power rails: the upper line (black, -) is 'bn' and the lower line (red, +) is 'bp'. Rail hole numbers are estimated from the image.

Pushbutton: side 1 (1.l/1.r) is the left column pair (column 4) and side 2 (2.l/2.r) is the right column pair (column 6), straddling the centre gap. Column 4 goes to 5V and column 6 to pin 2 and the resistor, which matches the schematic.
The pull-down resistor (10 kΩ, value=10000) shares column 6 with pin 2 on the same side of the button, and goes through a short black wire (column 9) to the ground rail.
The orange wire links button column 4 to the 5V rail, and the Arduino 5V and GND header sockets feed the two rails with red and black wires.
The USB cable and the sketch code (Serial.begin(9600), pinMode, digitalRead) are not part of the build graph.

The breadboard in the image labels the half nearest the power rails at the bottom as rows a-e and the upper half as f-j. I followed the catalogue naming: bank 't' = rows a-e (the lower half in the image) and bank 'b' = rows f-j (the upper half). The rails next to the a-e half (the lower rails in the image) are named tp (+) and tn (-).
Exact rail hole numbers (tp.1, tp.3, tn.1, tn.7) are estimated from the image. Any hole on the same rail is electrically equivalent.

The button straddles the centre gap in columns 4 and 6. I assumed the legs in one column are the internally joined pair. Side 1 is column 4, which goes to 5V through the orange wire. Side 2 is column 6, which goes to pin 2 and to the pull-down resistor.
The resistor is a 10k pull-down, stored as value=10000. It runs from column 6 (the pin 2 and button side 2 node) to column 9, and a black wire takes column 9 to the GND rail.
The red wire goes from 5V to the + rail. The black wire goes from the second GND pin (GND.2) to the - rail.
The LED on pin 13 is the board's built-in LED, so it is not a separate part.
